tasks.short: Analyse employment data and prepare required workforce reports.

steps.what: Export employee, position and absence records for the reporting period.
Reconcile identifiers, dates and organisational categories in the reporting workbook.
Calculate required totals, rates and comparisons using agreed definitions.
Interpret changes and assemble the report with explanatory notes.
Check explanations, disclosure scope and required report content.
Distribute the corrected report to authorised internal recipients.
Submit required external returns and retain the submission receipt.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled extracts from the {HCM}; a job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} validates records, calculates metrics and fills approved templates in the {DOCS}. The HR specialist adds explanations, and the {WORKFLOW} captures approval before internal distribution or supported filing to the {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports use different definitions, organisational mappings and recipient rules. Maintaining reliable connections often cost more than repeating the monthly workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting configuration and faster development make validation, template generation and connections cheaper to build. The calculations need no model.
tasks.still_hard: Historical reorganisations, inconsistent absence categories and changing filing specifications still need attention. GDPR limits disclosure; national rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why a metric moved, challenge misleading comparisons and decide which workforce issue deserves investigation.

ambition.what: Weekly staffing-risk review using vacancy and absence trends.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating changes and advising managers. Reporting automation grants no additional hiring, policy or disclosure authority.

reach.learn: Job grading, comparable groups and disclosure controls for small groups.

reach.task: Assess staffing risks against service demand.
reach.learn: Capacity planning and the difference between correlation and an actionable cause.

evidence.claim: Structured workforce reporting can use configured exports, deterministic validation and template generation.
Cross-system mappings and interpretation usually remain the main reporting exceptions.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates for a typical mid-size European employer.
The task includes internal reporting and periodic employment returns; not every reporting cycle includes filing.
Structured inputs support a deterministic design despite the prior identifying judgement as the hard part.
Estimates assume one main employee-record source and a small set of report templates.
Automated filing depends on a supported interface; otherwise portal entry remains human.
unknowns: Required reports, filing jurisdictions, deadlines and authorised recipients.
Current metric definitions and historical organisation mappings.
Available interfaces, credentials and export permissions.
Whether a national consultation or consent process applies.
Current data quality and correction ownership.
research_questions: Which filing formats and submission interfaces are currently supported?
Which national rules govern workforce reporting and employee consultation?
Can existing reporting configuration cover the required templates before custom code is built?
new_work: Review data exceptions and unexplained metric changes.
Maintain metric definitions, organisation mappings and report templates.
Check recipient permissions and submission failures.
Retest reports when source fields or filing specifications change.

tasks.short: Advise managers on recruiting and retention programmes.

steps.what: Clarify the management problem, affected workforce and constraints.
Review workforce trends for the groups named in the brief.
Read employee feedback and prior programme evaluations for recurring concerns.

loop.input: Approved employee feedback and programme evaluations, with source identifiers.
loop.output: Themes linked to supporting passages, conflicting views and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require valid source references; check sample coverage and remove identifying quotations.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass; unsupported themes go to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text concerns use varied language; fixed categories alone miss meaning and disagreement.

steps.what: Prepare programme options, expected mechanisms, costs and evaluation measures.

loop.input: Programme brief, reviewed evidence, approved option library and calculated costs.
loop.output: Option brief distinguishing evidence, assumptions, trade-offs and proposed evaluation measures.
loop.check: Recalculate costs deterministically, verify citations and require explicit labels for uncertain benefits.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or unresolved contradictions return to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover structure, but linking mixed evidence to management's question requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Discuss trade-offs and recommend a programme with management.
Approve programme scope, budget and evaluation criteria.
Record delivery owners, milestones and evaluation dates.

tasks.design: Configure a programme baseline from the {HCM}, and use approved material in the {DOCS} for bounded theme extraction and option drafting. People discuss and approve the recommendation; the {WORKFLOW} then creates milestones in the {PROJECT} and schedules evaluation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on local context and trust. Relevant feedback and previous evaluations are scattered, while programme costs and outcomes use inconsistent definitions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured metrics and small, source-linked reading and drafting loops reduce preparation. Faster development makes a reusable evidence pack affordable without automating the management conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Retention outcomes have many causes and appear slowly. GDPR applies to employee feedback; national rules may require consultation before programme changes, and individual worker evaluation can raise EU AI Act obligations [S17].
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unspoken concerns, challenge a manager's diagnosis and negotiate a programme employees will trust.

ambition.what: A quarterly retention-pilot evaluation clinic for line managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time testing explanations and coaching managers, with less evidence assembly. Programme and budget approval rights remain with the HR manager.

reach.learn: Pilot design, comparison groups and budget trade-offs.

reach.task: Design development interventions for retention problems.
reach.learn: Skill diagnosis and evidence that distinguishes training needs from management problems.

reach.task: Assess employee consultation requirements for programme changes.
reach.learn: Collective agreements and applicable national consultation procedures.

evidence.claim: Configured workforce metrics can reduce preparation for programme advice.
Source-linked theme extraction and drafting are plausible bounded model uses; local accuracy requires testing.
Management advice and programme approval still require contextual judgement and conversation.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.
The programme baseline uses aggregate workforce data rather than individual flight-risk scores.
Feedback was collected for a compatible purpose and is available with suitable access restrictions.
The low-drudgery prior supports keeping diagnosis, discussion and programme approval human.
Budget approval sits with the HR manager in this typical workflow.
unknowns: The management question and programme budget.
Available feedback, its collection purpose and retention limits.
Previous programme evaluations and usable comparison groups.
Actual programme approval rights.
Applicable national rules and collective agreements.
research_questions: How reliably does theme extraction preserve dissent and minority concerns in the languages used?
Which evaluation method can distinguish programme effects from wider workforce changes?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed programme?
new_work: Review feedback themes for omissions and identifying details.
Verify option evidence and cost assumptions.
Maintain the approved option library and evaluation templates.
Track pilot outcomes and investigate unintended effects.

tasks.short: Develop and implement recruiting strategies for current and future staffing needs.

steps.what: Agree staffing demand, role priorities and hiring constraints with managers.
Review vacancy pipelines, source performance and hiring delays.
Calculate channel costs, hiring capacity and timing scenarios.
Choose channels, sequencing and contingencies against staffing priorities.
Write the recruiting plan, responsibilities and campaign briefs.

loop.input: Selected approach, calculated scenarios, approved role requirements and plan template.
loop.output: Recruiting plan and channel briefs using only approved commitments and requirements.
loop.check: Validate budget and dates deterministically; compare requirements and claims with approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unclear requirements return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Channel briefs need contextual wording; a fixed template cannot express every approved role and approach.

steps.what: Approve the recruiting plan, spending limits and campaign scope.
Set up approved vacancies, recruitment stages and supported channel distribution.
Brief recruitment partners and resolve delivery questions.
Track channel results and flag departures from the approved plan.

tasks.design: Configure pipeline and channel reporting in the {ATS}, and use deterministic scenario calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to compare costs and capacity. A bounded drafting loop prepares plans in the {DOCS}; approved vacancies use existing {ATS} distribution, while people choose the strategy and brief partners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel attribution is incomplete, staffing demand changes and campaign execution crosses several teams. Generic recruitment configuration does not choose priorities or resolve scarce-skill trade-offs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and distribution features cover much of the execution. Faster development lowers the cost of scenario tools, with a small drafting loop for campaign briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Past channel conversion rates may not predict future hiring. GDPR applies to candidate data; screening or candidate evaluation would introduce a separate EU AI Act assessment [S17] and GDPR Article 22 test [S20].
tasks.human_edge: Choose realistic hiring priorities, recognise labour-market constraints and secure commitments from managers and partners.

ambition.what: Fortnightly recruitment-channel reallocation reviews within the approved budget.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time calculating scenarios and setting up campaigns, and more time adjusting priorities with managers. Budget reallocation rights require explicit delegation; automation itself grants none.

reach.task: Translate workforce plans into hiring investment choices.
reach.learn: Scenario planning, hiring capacity and budget delegation.

reach.task: Assess whether proposed pay ranges support hard-to-fill recruitment.
reach.learn: Job evaluation, pay positioning and aggregate offer-acceptance analysis.

reach.task: Compare internal development with external recruitment for skill gaps.
reach.learn: Time to proficiency and internal mobility constraints.

evidence.claim: Recruiting scenario calculations, campaign configuration and monitoring can largely use deterministic technology.
Textkernel offers CV parsing and matching, showing that recruitment inputs can be structured; it does not establish strategy automation.
Selecting channels and negotiating delivery commitments remain contextual human work.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are estimates for recurring recruitment planning.
The {ATS} supports vacancy templates, configurable stages and some channel distribution.
This design does not rank candidates or make screening decisions.
Partner briefing stays within existing agreements; new contracts need a separate approval workflow.
The creative-work prior does not remove the deterministic arithmetic and configuration steps exposed by decomposition.
unknowns: Supported recruitment channels and distribution interfaces.
Completeness of source attribution, channel costs and recruitment-stage timestamps.
Actual hiring capacity and staffing priorities.
Who may approve spending, publication and budget reallocation.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which campaign actions can existing recruitment configuration perform?
How should scenario estimates express uncertainty for channels with little history?
Would any proposed extension evaluate candidates and therefore require additional EU AI Act assessment?
new_work: Maintain channel rates, conversion assumptions and capacity limits.
Review generated campaign briefs and publication details.
Investigate attribution gaps and campaign exceptions.
Revisit scenario assumptions when labour-market conditions change.

tasks.short: Administer employee benefit eligibility, enrolments, changes and reconciliations.

steps.what: Record employee enrolment or benefit-change requests and relevant life events.
Check supporting documents for required facts and missing evidence.

loop.input: Only the supporting documents required for the benefit case and evidence checklist.
loop.output: Required dates and facts with source locations, plus missing or conflicting evidence.
loop.check: Validate formats and chronology; require source locations and human review of ambiguous facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or conflicting evidence returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: External proofs have varied layouts and wording; structured forms cannot replace every required document.

steps.what: Apply plan eligibility, contribution and effective-date rules.
Resolve ambiguous eligibility, adverse decisions and requests outside standard rules.
Explain options, resolve employee concerns and confirm the employee's choice.
Submit approved enrolments or changes through the benefit administrator's portal.
Update payroll deductions and taxable benefit entries from confirmed changes.
Match administrator statements and invoices against enrolments and payroll deductions.

tasks.design: Configure benefit intake and eligibility assessments in the {HCM}, with a bounded document-extraction loop using restricted material in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and captures approval before supported submissions to the {PARTNER_PORTAL}; deterministic connections update the {PAYROLL} and reconcile statements with invoices from the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Benefit administrators, employee records and payroll use different formats and effective dates. Supporting evidence and exceptions make a single unattended workflow unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing benefit configuration handles standard rules, while cheaper integrations connect confirmed changes. Bounded extraction can reduce document reading without deciding eligibility.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, collective agreements and administrator corrections remain difficult. GDPR protections for health and other special-category data apply where present; significant automated benefit decisions need an Article 22 assessment [S20], and national consultation rules vary.
tasks.human_edge: Support employees during sensitive life events, explain consequences clearly and resolve disputed entitlements fairly.

ambition.what: A benefits continuity check before employees begin extended leave.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rekeying enrolments to resolving difficult cases and preventing interrupted coverage. Benefit-policy and payment authority do not change.

reach.learn: Payroll cut-offs, effective dates and correction procedures.

reach.task: Review benefit utilisation and plan design.
reach.learn: Aggregate utilisation analysis, plan economics and privacy limits.

reach.task: Triage benefit requests and missing evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, secure handling and escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Standard benefit eligibility and contribution rules can often be configured in employee-record systems.
Confirmed enrolment changes and payroll deductions can be connected and reconciled deterministically.
Varied supporting documents can use bounded extraction with source checks and human exception handling.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Routine requests can move to employee self-service without transferring difficult cases to employees.
The {HCM} can represent the main benefit rules; unsupported rules need deterministic code.
Administrator interfaces are not assumed from the strong API prior and require confirmation.
Machine eligibility outputs are assessments; adverse or ambiguous decisions remain human.
Build estimates cover one main administrator and one payroll interface; additional plans increase effort.
The enrolment gate confirms the employee's recorded choice and validates external changes.
unknowns: Benefit plans, administrator interfaces and supported submission formats.
Applicable national rules, collective agreements and plan eligibility terms.
Which evidence contains health or other special-category data.
Payroll cut-offs, tax treatment and retroactive correction procedures.
Who may decide exceptions and approve administrator submissions.
Required employee consultation, access approvals and existing data-protection assessments.
research_questions: Can current benefit configuration cover effective dates and retroactive changes?
Which administrator interfaces return reliable acknowledgements and support duplicate prevention?
What data-protection assessment is needed for the proposed document processing?
Which national rules govern consultation and disputed benefit entitlements?
new_work: Review extracted facts and ambiguous eligibility assessments.
Resolve failed submissions and missing administrator confirmations.
Maintain benefit rules, contribution tables and effective-date mappings.
Retest changes to benefit plans and payroll interfaces.

role.altitude: The HR specialist spends less time assembling records, reports and campaign paperwork, and more time investigating workforce issues and supporting managers and employees. Existing approval rights remain; any delegated pilot or budget authority must be agreed explicitly.
reach: Support HR managers with workforce scenarios and programme evaluations.
Support compensation and benefits specialists with aggregate analysis and benefit exceptions.
Work with payroll clerks on benefit corrections and effective-date controls.
Work with training and development specialists on internal development alternatives to recruitment.
Consult labor relations specialists on applicable national consultation requirements.
skills_to_grow: Workforce metric definitions and data-quality diagnosis.
Deterministic rule design and acceptance criteria.
Source checking for bounded reading and drafting loops.
Programme evaluation and cautious interpretation of workforce trends.
GDPR, relevant EU AI Act scope and national employment rules.
Manager coaching, employee conversations and fair exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a workforce advisory service combining regular staffing-risk reviews, recruitment-channel reviews, retention-pilot evaluations and benefits continuity checks. Seek explicit authority to run small approved pilots and recommend reallocations within defined budgets, while consequential employee decisions remain meaningfully human.
